title: A Salt for the Crown Revisited
premise: Jude Dunmore, a salt-sworn mercenary of a silent god, discovers her name and today's date in the Century Codex, a prophecy book hidden in a smuggler's cache. The prophecy names her the 'Saltbride' who must reforge the broken covenant between the mortal realms and the drowned court beneath Thornfell, or the usurper Kaelen Voss will claim both worlds. Pursued by Voss's inquisitors, Jude gathers a found family of heretics, smugglers, and one exiled drowned-court heir, Tam, with whom she falls in love against every vow she holds. At the drowned court she learns the covenant broke because the gods chose silence to hide a truth: the crown itself was forged from the covenant's first sacrifice. In the end Jude refuses the prophecy's terms, shatters the crown, and reforges the covenant as an equal bargain rather than a bride-price, saving the free cities and choosing Tam and her found family over both duty and crown.
about_author: Wendell Iversen is the pen name of a former cartographer's apprentice from the northern fjord country who now writes fantasy from a converted lighthouse. Their work is known for salt-bleaked landscapes, stubborn found families, and gods with inconvenient silences.

chapters.title: The Date in the Margins
chapters.summary: Jude Dunmore, guiding a smuggler's caravan through Thornfell, raids a waystation cache and finds the Century Codex, which names her and tonight's date. Her patron god, the Silent Tide, has not answered a prayer in nine years. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: unease curdling into dread as the impossible becomes personal.

chapters.title: Inquisitors at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: Usurper Kaelen Voss's inquisitors burn the waystation hunting the Codex, and Jude's caravan master is taken. She escapes with the book and a half-dead stranger, Tam, who recognizes the drowned-court sigil on its cover. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: first taste of the cost of knowing.

chapters.title: What Tam Remembers of Drowning
chapters.summary: Tam reveals she is exiled heir of the drowned court beneath Thornfell, banished when the covenant between realms broke a century ago. She confirms the Codex's prophecy: a Saltbride must reforge it or both realms fall to Voss. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: grief for a homeland that hates her.

chapters.title: The Free City of Brack
chapters.summary: The pair reach Brack, where Jude's old mercenary company, the Saltcloaks, has gone half-heretic under her former sergeant, Ossa Vane. Ossa agrees to shelter them but warns the Codex makes Jude a target for every crown and creed. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the first fragile warmth of belonging.

chapters.title: Reading the Prophecy Backwards
chapters.summary: Brack's blind archivist, Mother Quill, deciphers the Codex: the covenant was sealed by a sacrifice the gods hid behind their silence, and the Saltbride's role is a bride-price, not an honor. Jude refuses; the prophecy begins fulfilling itself anyway. POV: Mother Quill. Emotional beat: horror at destiny's fine print.

chapters.title: Ossa's Bargain
chapters.summary: Voss's army crosses the Thorn passes; Ossa offers the Saltcloaks' protection only if Jude surrenders the Codex to sell to Voss. Jude, betrayed, flees with Tam and Quill through smuggler roads only she knows. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: found family fractured by survival.

chapters.title: The Road Under the Mountain
chapters.summary: In the deep roads, the Codex's magic begins rewriting itself around Jude's choices, and drowned-court wardens ambush them. Tam bargains passage by naming herself heir, and the wardens kneel to her, not Jude. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: the ache of being loved by a home she was cast out of.

chapters.title: Salt Prayers
chapters.summary: Jude attempts the old rites to reach the Silent Tide and receives, for the first time in nine years, an answer: a single drowned word. Quill interprets it as a warning, not a blessing. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: hope that feels more like a trap springing shut.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Court
chapters.summary: In Voss's war camp, inquisitor Serah Dane presents the stolen Codex fragment Ossa sold, and Voss reveals he wants the covenant reforged under his crown, with Jude as the sacrifice. POV: Serah Dane. Emotional beat: a true believer's first crack of doubt.

chapters.title: The Drowned Gate
chapters.summary: The company reaches the Drowned Gate, the threshold to the court beneath the sea, and must pay a toll in memories. Quill gives hers willingly, forgetting her life's work to open the way. POV: Quill. Emotional beat: sacrifice as an act of faith in others.

chapters.title: The Court of Salt and Pearl
chapters.summary: In the drowned court, Tam's exile is revoked and she is crowned heir, but the regent, her aunt Nerissa, intends to fulfill the prophecy by binding Jude to the covenant at the next tide. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: homecoming poisoned by duty.

chapters.title: A Bride for the Covenant
chapters.summary: Jude learns the full rite: the Saltbride's heart becomes the seal, and the Silent Tide's silence was grief for the last sacrifice, its own chosen. Jude and Tam, half in love, plan to refuse the rite together. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: love chosen in the shadow of an altar.

chapters.title: Nerissa's Tide
chapters.summary: Nerissa moves the rite up, imprisoning Tam as a collaborator and preparing Jude by force. The drowned court splits, wardens who love Tam turning against the regent. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: rage and resolve as the court chooses sides.

chapters.title: The Escape from the Pearl Hall
chapters.summary: Jude breaks free with help from a repentant Serah Dane, who arrived as Voss's envoy and defects. They free Tam, but Quill's memory-toll proves fatal, and she dies naming them her family. POV: Serah Dane. Emotional beat: conversion through witness; grief for a chosen mother.

chapters.title: Voss at the Gate
chapters.summary: Voss's armies breach the Drowned Gate with a stolen fragment of the crown, and the drowned court's defenses fail. Nerissa, desperate, begs Tam to complete the rite. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: terror as every road converges on the altar.

chapters.title: The Truth in the Codex
chapters.summary: The Codex, rewritten by Jude's refusals, reveals its final page: the crown of the free cities was forged from the covenant's first sacrifice, and the Silent Tide went silent to hide this from both realms. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning the war itself is a lie.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: At the tide-peak rite, Jude stands at the altar before gods, court, and army, and publicly refuses the prophecy, declaring no covenant built on a bride-price will hold. The Silent Tide finally speaks fully, confirming her. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: defiance as an act of love.

chapters.title: The Shattering of the Crown
chapters.summary: Voss attacks the rite to seize the covenant for himself; in the battle Tam and Jude fight together, and Jude shatters the crown-forged-from-sacrifice, breaking Voss's claim and the old covenant at once. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: fury and partnership, two people fighting as one.

chapters.title: A New Bargain
chapters.summary: With the crown broken, Jude offers the Silent Tide a covenant of exchange rather than sacrifice: memory for memory, salt for salt, freely given. The Tide accepts, and the seas calm; Voss's armies, their mandate dissolved, rout. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: exhausted, hard-won peace.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Ossa Vane
chapters.summary: Ossa, who sold them out, comes to Brack to kneel; the surviving Saltcloaks must decide her fate. Jude chooses exile over execution, and the company re-founds itself under new salt-oaths. POV: Ossa Vane. Emotional beat: forgiveness that does not forget.

chapters.title: Two Courts, One Tide
chapters.summary: Tam, now queen of a drowned court remade as an open realm, and Jude, no longer a bride but a covenant-keeper, formalize the new bargain between realms at the Drowned Gate. Serah Dane becomes the first inquisitor turned envoy. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: inheritance rewritten into something worth keeping.

chapters.title: The Answered Prayer
chapters.summary: One year on, Jude prays at a Thornfell waystation and the Silent Tide answers plainly, a god no longer silent. She walks the smuggler roads home to Tam, the Codex's final line now reading simply: 'and she chose.' POV: Jude. Emotional beat: quiet joy; love and duty finally the same road.
